title.en: Lost Medicaid in Florida 2026? Your Next Steps Guide
title.es: Perdio Medicaid en Florida 2026? Guia de Proximos Pasos

description.en: Lost Florida Medicaid in 2026? You have 90 days to enroll in ACA marketplace. Florida is a non-expansion state. Learn your options and the coverage gap.
description.es: Perdio Medicaid en Florida? Tiene 90 dias para inscribirse. Florida no expandio Medicaid, conozca sus opciones, la brecha de cobertura y como solicitar seguro.

h1.en: Lost Medicaid in Florida? Here Are Your Next Steps in 2026
h1.es: Perdio Medicaid en Florida? Aqui Estan Sus Proximos Pasos en 2026

subhero.en: Florida did not expand Medicaid under the ACA, which makes your options different from most states. You have 90 days from your Florida Medicaid termination date to enroll in ACA marketplace coverage, but the coverage gap is real for many Floridians under 100% FPL.
subhero.es: Florida no expandio Medicaid bajo el ACA, lo que hace que sus opciones sean diferentes a la mayoria de los estados. Tiene 90 dias desde la fecha de terminacion de su Medicaid de Florida para inscribirse en cobertura del mercado ACA.

heading.en: You have 90 days from your Florida Medicaid termination date
heading.es: Tiene 90 dias desde la fecha de terminacion de su Medicaid de Florida

body.en: Your 90-day Special Enrollment Period runs from your Florida Medicaid termination date through 90 days later, for example, if your coverage ended June 1, 2026, your SEP window closes August 30, 2026. Miss that deadline and you must wait until the next Open Enrollment (November 1, 2026 through January 15, 2027 for 2027 coverage). Florida KidCare for children is year-round and has no enrollment deadline.
body.es: Su Periodo de Inscripcion Especial de 90 dias corre desde la fecha de terminacion de su Medicaid de Florida, por ejemplo, si su cobertura termino el 1 de junio de 2026, su ventana SEP cierra el 30 de agosto de 2026. Florida KidCare para ninos es todo el ano y no tiene fecha limite de inscripcion.

label.es: Reinscripcion en Medicaid (si el ingreso recalifica)

quickAnswer.en: Losing Florida Medicaid in 2026 gives you a 90-day Special Enrollment Period to enroll in an ACA marketplace plan at healthcare.gov. Florida has NOT expanded Medicaid under the ACA, so non-parent adults earning under 100% of the Federal Poverty Level ($15,960 single) fall into the Florida coverage gap and may not qualify for Marketplace subsidies either. If your income is between 100% and 400% FPL ($15,960 to $63,840 for a single person in 2026), you qualify for ACA premium tax credits. Children in your household may still qualify for Florida KidCare (CHIP) at up to 300% FPL regardless of your eligibility. Act quickly: the 90-day SEP clock starts from your Medicaid termination date.
quickAnswer.es: Perder Medicaid de Florida en 2026 le da un Periodo de Inscripcion Especial de 90 dias para inscribirse en un plan del mercado ACA en healthcare.gov. Florida NO ha expandido Medicaid bajo el ACA, por lo que los adultos no padres con ingresos bajo el 100% del Nivel Federal de Pobreza ($15,960 individual) caen en la brecha de cobertura de Florida. Si su ingreso esta entre el 100% y el 400% FPL, califica para creditos fiscales del ACA. Los ninos en su hogar pueden calificar para Florida KidCare (CHIP) hasta el 300% FPL. Actue rapido: el reloj de 90 dias comienza desde la fecha de terminacion de su Medicaid.

introParagraphs.en: Losing Florida Medicaid coverage is especially complicated because Florida is one of 10 states that has not expanded Medicaid under the Affordable Care Act. Most states cover adults earning up to 138% of the Federal Poverty Level, but Florida Medicaid for parents only reaches approximately 17% FPL (about $355 per month for a single parent in 2026), and non-parent adults between ages 19 and 64 without a qualifying disability are categorically excluded from Florida Medicaid regardless of income. That structural gap means that when you lose Florida Medicaid, the path forward depends entirely on what category you were in, parent, pregnant woman, child, person with disability, or person over 65, and what your current household income is. This guide gives you the Florida-specific decision tree so you know exactly which door to walk through within your 90-day Special Enrollment Period window.
introParagraphs.es: Perder la cobertura de Medicaid de Florida es especialmente complicado porque Florida es uno de los 10 estados que no ha expandido Medicaid bajo la Ley de Cuidado de Salud a Bajo Precio. La mayoria de los estados cubren a adultos con ingresos de hasta el 138% del Nivel Federal de Pobreza, pero el Medicaid de Florida para padres solo llega aproximadamente al 17% FPL (cerca de $355 al mes para un padre soltero en 2026), y los adultos sin hijos entre 19 y 64 anos sin discapacidad calificadora estan categoricamente excluidos del Medicaid de Florida independientemente de sus ingresos. Esta guia le da el arbol de decision especifico de Florida para que sepa exactamente que camino tomar dentro de su ventana de Periodo de Inscripcion Especial de 90 dias.

introParagraphs.en: Florida uses its own Medicaid portal, MyACCESS at myaccess.myflfamilies.com, administered by the Florida Department of Children and Families. The Florida marketplace runs through the federally-facilitated platform at healthcare.gov, Florida does not have a state-based exchange. In 2026, the enhanced premium tax credits from the American Rescue Plan Act and the Inflation Reduction Act expired January 1, 2026, so marketplace costs are higher than in 2023 through 2025 for people near the top of the subsidy range. Standard premium tax credits still apply for incomes between 100% and 400% FPL. Approximately 800,000 Floridians fall into the coverage gap, earning too much for Florida Medicaid but too little (under 100% FPL, about $15,060 for a single person) to qualify for marketplace subsidies. If you are in that gap, this guide explains your limited but real options, including community health centers and Florida KidCare for your children.
introParagraphs.es: Florida usa su propio portal de Medicaid, MyACCESS en myaccess.myflfamilies.com, administrado por el Departamento de Ninos y Familias de Florida. El mercado de Florida opera a traves de la plataforma federal en healthcare.gov, Florida no tiene un intercambio basado en el estado. En 2026, los creditos fiscales de prima mejorados del ARPA y la IRA expiraron el 1 de enero de 2026, por lo que los costos del mercado son mas altos que en 2023 a 2025. Los creditos fiscales estandar aun aplican para ingresos entre el 100% y el 400% FPL. Aproximadamente 800,000 floridanos caen en la brecha de cobertura, ganando demasiado para el Medicaid de Florida pero muy poco (bajo el 100% FPL) para calificar para subsidios del mercado.

name.en: Read your Florida Medicaid termination notice immediately
name.es: Lea su aviso de terminacion de Medicaid de Florida de inmediato

text.en: Florida's Agency for Health Care Administration (AHCA) or DCF must send written notice before terminating coverage. Check your MyACCESS account at myaccess.myflfamilies.com for the exact termination date, the stated reason (income change, paperwork, work requirement, or eligibility category), and the appeal deadline. Your 90-day SEP clock starts from the termination date on the notice, not the date you read it.
text.es: La Agencia para la Administracion del Cuidado de la Salud de Florida (AHCA) o el DCF debe enviar un aviso escrito antes de terminar la cobertura. Verifique su cuenta MyACCESS en myaccess.myflfamilies.com para obtener la fecha exacta de terminacion, la razon indicada y la fecha limite de apelacion. Su reloj de SEP de 90 dias comienza desde la fecha de terminacion en el aviso.

name.en: File a Florida Medicaid appeal if the termination looks wrong
name.es: Presente una apelacion de Medicaid de Florida si la terminacion parece incorrecta

text.en: Call DCF at (850) 300-4323 or submit a fair hearing request through MyACCESS before the appeal deadline stated in your notice. Florida allows 90 days from the notice to request a fair hearing. If you request a hearing before your coverage ends, you may be entitled to continuation of benefits during the appeal. File the appeal AND apply for ACA marketplace coverage simultaneously, do not wait for the appeal outcome to protect yourself from a coverage gap.
text.es: Llame al DCF al (850) 300-4323 o presente una solicitud de audiencia justa a traves de MyACCESS antes de la fecha limite de apelacion indicada en su aviso. Florida permite 90 dias desde el aviso para solicitar una audiencia justa. Presente la apelacion Y solicite cobertura del mercado ACA al mismo tiempo para evitar una brecha de cobertura.

name.en: Determine your income position relative to Florida's thresholds
name.es: Determine su posicion de ingresos con respecto a los umbrales de Florida

text.en: Check your 2026 projected household income against these three Florida-specific thresholds: (1) Under 100% FPL ($15,060 single, $31,200 family of 4), you fall in the Florida coverage gap; Florida Medicaid for adults is only available to parents under approximately 17% FPL or people with qualifying disabilities; (2) Between 100% and 400% FPL, ACA marketplace subsidies apply and Florida Blue, Ambetter, or Oscar Health plans may cost $0 to $200 per month with the standard premium tax credit; (3) Above 400% FPL ($60,240 single), the 2026 subsidy cliff means you pay full premium with no ACA subsidy. Use the federal poverty level calculator at healthcare.gov to confirm your percentage.
text.es: Verifique su ingreso proyectado del hogar en 2026 frente a estos tres umbrales especificos de Florida: (1) Bajo el 100% FPL ($15,060 individual, $31,200 familia de 4), cae en la brecha de cobertura de Florida; (2) Entre el 100% y el 400% FPL, aplican subsidios del mercado ACA y los planes de Florida Blue, Ambetter u Oscar Health pueden costar de $0 a $200 al mes; (3) Por encima del 400% FPL ($60,240 individual), el acantilado de subsidios 2026 significa que paga la prima completa sin subsidio del ACA.

name.en: Enroll in an ACA marketplace plan at healthcare.gov within 90 days
name.es: Inscribase en un plan del mercado ACA en healthcare.gov dentro de los 90 dias

text.en: Log in or create an account at healthcare.gov and select 'I lost qualifying health coverage' as your qualifying life event. Choose Medicaid or CHIP as the type of coverage lost and enter your Florida Medicaid termination date. You have 90 days from that date to pick a plan. Compare Silver plans first if your income is between 100% and 250% FPL, cost-sharing reductions on Silver plans lower your deductible to as low as $150 and your out-of-pocket maximum to under $3,000 per year. Florida has 16 insurance carriers on the marketplace in 2026, including Florida Blue, Ambetter, Oscar Health, Molina Healthcare, and UnitedHealthcare.
text.es: Inicie sesion o cree una cuenta en healthcare.gov y seleccione 'Perdi cobertura medica calificada' como su evento calificador. Elija Medicaid o CHIP como el tipo de cobertura perdida e ingrese la fecha de terminacion de su Medicaid de Florida. Tiene 90 dias desde esa fecha para elegir un plan. Compare los planes Silver primero si su ingreso esta entre el 100% y el 250% FPL, las reducciones en la participacion de costos en los planes Silver reducen su deducible a tan solo $150 y su maximo de gastos de bolsillo a menos de $3,000 al ano.

name.en: Apply for Florida KidCare to protect your children's coverage
name.es: Solicite Florida KidCare para proteger la cobertura de sus hijos

text.en: Florida KidCare is Florida's CHIP program and covers children under 19 at incomes up to 300% FPL ($99,000 for a family of 4 in 2026). KidCare enrollment is year-round with no SEP deadline. Apply at floridakidcare.org. Families between 133% and 200% FPL pay $15 to $20 per month for all children in the household. Even if you as an adult fall into the Florida coverage gap, your children may qualify for free or low-cost KidCare coverage immediately.
text.es: Florida KidCare es el programa CHIP de Florida y cubre a ninos menores de 19 con ingresos de hasta el 300% FPL ($99,000 para una familia de 4 en 2026). La inscripcion en KidCare es todo el ano sin fecha limite. Solicite en floridakidcare.org. Las familias entre el 133% y el 200% FPL pagan de $15 a $20 al mes por todos los ninos del hogar.

name.en: Submit proof of Florida Medicaid loss and complete your marketplace enrollment
name.es: Presente prueba de perdida de Medicaid de Florida y complete su inscripcion en el mercado

text.en: Upload your Florida Medicaid termination letter or DCF notice to healthcare.gov within 30 days of selecting a plan. Coverage typically starts the first day of the month after you complete enrollment. Do not let the 90-day window expire without a plan selected. If you are in the Florida coverage gap (under 100% FPL, ineligible for marketplace subsidies), contact a Navigator or a Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC), Florida has over 50 FQHC locations that provide sliding-scale care regardless of insurance status. Call 211 to find the nearest FQHC in Florida.
text.es: Suba su carta de terminacion de Medicaid de Florida o aviso del DCF a healthcare.gov dentro de los 30 dias posteriores a seleccionar un plan. La cobertura generalmente comienza el primer dia del mes despues de que complete la inscripcion. Si esta en la brecha de cobertura de Florida (bajo el 100% FPL), contacte a un Navegador o un Centro de Salud Comunitario Calificado Federalmente (FQHC), Florida tiene mas de 50 ubicaciones de FQHC que brindan atencion a escala de honorarios reducidos independientemente del estado de seguro.

intro.en: The most costly mistakes Floridians make after losing Medicaid coverage in 2026:
intro.es: Los errores mas costosos que los floridanos cometen despues de perder la cobertura de Medicaid en 2026:

items.en: Assuming the 90-day SEP works the same as the standard 60-day SEP. Loss of Medicaid gives you 90 days, but the clock starts on the termination date shown in your DCF or AHCA notice, not when you discover the loss.
items.es: Asumir que el SEP de 90 dias funciona igual que el SEP estandar de 60 dias. La perdida de Medicaid le da 90 dias, pero el reloj comienza en la fecha de terminacion que aparece en su aviso del DCF o AHCA, no cuando descubre la perdida.

items.en: Not recognizing the Florida coverage gap. Because Florida has not expanded Medicaid, adults under 100% FPL ($15,060 single in 2026) who are not parents, pregnant, or disabled cannot get Florida Medicaid OR marketplace subsidies. Applying at healthcare.gov when income is under 100% FPL will result in a denial of subsidies, not a referral to Medicaid expansion.
items.es: No reconocer la brecha de cobertura de Florida. Debido a que Florida no ha expandido Medicaid, los adultos bajo el 100% FPL que no son padres, mujeres embarazadas o discapacitados no pueden obtener Medicaid de Florida NI subsidios del mercado. Solicitar en healthcare.gov cuando los ingresos estan bajo el 100% FPL resultara en un rechazo de subsidios.

items.en: Waiting to apply for marketplace coverage until after the Medicaid appeal is resolved. Appeals can take 30 to 90 days or longer. Apply for an ACA marketplace plan through healthcare.gov at the same time as your appeal, if the appeal succeeds and Medicaid is reinstated, you can cancel the marketplace plan.
items.es: Esperar para solicitar cobertura del mercado hasta que se resuelva la apelacion de Medicaid. Las apelaciones pueden tomar de 30 a 90 dias o mas. Solicite un plan del mercado ACA a traves de healthcare.gov al mismo tiempo que su apelacion.

items.en: Forgetting that Florida KidCare (CHIP) is a separate program for children. Even if you as an adult are stuck in the Florida coverage gap, your children under 19 can enroll in Florida KidCare year-round at floridakidcare.org at incomes up to 300% FPL ($99,000 family of 4 in 2026).
items.es: Olvidar que Florida KidCare (CHIP) es un programa separado para ninos. Incluso si usted como adulto esta atrapado en la brecha de cobertura de Florida, sus hijos menores de 19 pueden inscribirse en Florida KidCare todo el ano en floridakidcare.org con ingresos de hasta el 300% FPL.

items.en: Enrolling in a short-term health plan instead of an ACA marketplace plan. Short-term plans sold in Florida are not ACA-compliant, can deny coverage for pre-existing conditions, and do not count as qualifying coverage under HIPAA. An ACA Silver plan with subsidies is almost always a better choice if your income is between 100% and 400% FPL.
items.es: Inscribirse en un plan de salud a corto plazo en lugar de un plan del mercado ACA. Los planes a corto plazo vendidos en Florida no cumplen con el ACA, pueden negar cobertura por condiciones preexistentes y no cuentan como cobertura calificada bajo HIPAA. Un plan Silver del ACA con subsidios casi siempre es una mejor opcion.

heading.en: ACA Marketplace vs. Florida Coverage Gap: Which Situation Are You In?
heading.es: Mercado ACA vs. Brecha de Cobertura de Florida: En Que Situacion Se Encuentra?

paragraphs.en: Florida's non-expansion status creates two completely different situations for people who lose Florida Medicaid in 2026. Adults with income between 100% and 400% FPL ($15,060 to $60,240 for a single person) can access ACA marketplace plans at healthcare.gov with standard premium tax credits, making Silver plans $0 to $200 per month for most people in that income band. Cost-sharing reductions on Silver plans apply for incomes under 250% FPL ($37,650 single), cutting deductibles to as low as $150 and out-of-pocket maximums to under $3,000. Florida Blue, Ambetter, Oscar Health, and Molina Healthcare are the main carriers across most Florida counties in 2026. Run a quote at healthcare.gov to see actual plan costs by ZIP code and household size.
paragraphs.es: El estatus de no expansion de Florida crea dos situaciones completamente diferentes para las personas que pierden Medicaid de Florida en 2026. Los adultos con ingresos entre el 100% y el 400% FPL ($15,060 a $60,240 para una persona sola) pueden acceder a planes del mercado ACA en healthcare.gov con creditos fiscales de prima estandar, lo que hace que los planes Silver cuesten de $0 a $200 al mes. Las reducciones en la participacion de costos en los planes Silver aplican para ingresos bajo el 250% FPL ($37,650 individual), reduciendo los deducibles a tan solo $150.

paragraphs.en: Adults in the Florida coverage gap, earning under 100% FPL ($15,060 single in 2026) while not qualifying as a parent, pregnant woman, or person with a disability, face a harder path. Florida Medicaid for non-disabled adults without children has essentially no income pathway, and the ACA marketplace does not offer subsidies below 100% FPL in non-expansion states. Three practical options exist for people in this gap: (1) Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs) across Florida provide primary care on a sliding-fee scale regardless of insurance status, call 211 to locate the nearest FQHC; (2) Emergency Medicaid covers true medical emergencies even for people otherwise ineligible; (3) if income rises above 100% FPL at any point during the year, a qualifying life event or mid-year income report to healthcare.gov can trigger a Special Enrollment Period for ACA marketplace coverage.
paragraphs.es: Los adultos en la brecha de cobertura de Florida, que ganan bajo el 100% FPL ($15,060 individual en 2026) sin calificar como padres, mujeres embarazadas o personas con discapacidad, enfrentan un camino mas dificil. Tres opciones practicas existen para las personas en esta brecha: (1) los Centros de Salud Comunitarios Calificados Federalmente (FQHC) en Florida brindan atencion primaria en una escala de honorarios reducidos independientemente del estado de seguro, llame al 211 para localizar el FQHC mas cercano; (2) el Medicaid de emergencia cubre emergencias medicas verdaderas; (3) si los ingresos suben por encima del 100% FPL en cualquier momento, puede activarse un Periodo de Inscripcion Especial para cobertura del mercado ACA.

heading.en: Florida Medicaid Eligibility by Category in 2026
heading.es: Elegibilidad de Medicaid de Florida por Categoria en 2026

paragraphs.en: Florida Medicaid in 2026 covers several distinct eligibility categories, each with its own income limit. Parents and caretaker relatives: income up to approximately 17% FPL (about $355 per month for a single parent in 2026). Pregnant women: income up to 191% FPL ($28,749 for a single pregnant woman in 2026). Children up to age 18: income up to 214% FPL through Medicaid plus KidCare CHIP. Adults age 65 or older: separate SSI-linked income rules apply. People with qualifying disabilities receiving SSI or SSDI: separate eligibility pathway. Non-parent adults aged 19 to 64 without disabilities: categorically excluded from Florida Medicaid regardless of income. If you lost Medicaid from one of the covered categories, for example, a child who aged out or a parent whose income changed, you may be able to re-apply to the same or a different category if your circumstances qualify.
paragraphs.es: El Medicaid de Florida en 2026 cubre varias categorias de elegibilidad distintas. Padres y parientes cuidadores: ingresos hasta aproximadamente el 17% FPL (cerca de $355 al mes para un padre soltero en 2026). Mujeres embarazadas: ingresos hasta el 191% FPL ($28,749 para una mujer embarazada soltera en 2026). Ninos hasta 18 anos: ingresos hasta el 214% FPL a traves de Medicaid mas KidCare CHIP. Adultos sin hijos de 19 a 64 anos sin discapacidades: excluidos categoricamente de Medicaid de Florida independientemente de sus ingresos.

paragraphs.en: Florida implemented a redesigned Statewide Medicaid Managed Care (SMMC 3.0) program as of February 2025, which moved most Medicaid recipients into managed care plans. If your Florida Medicaid was terminated during or after the SMMC 3.0 transition, the termination reason matters for your appeal. Administrative errors during managed care plan transitions have been a known source of incorrect terminations. Request your complete case file from DCF at (850) 300-4323 before filing your appeal to confirm whether the termination was based on an eligibility determination or a data-transfer error.
paragraphs.es: Florida implemento un programa rediseñado de Cuidado Administrado de Medicaid Estatal (SMMC 3.0) a partir de febrero de 2025, que mueve a la mayoria de los beneficiarios de Medicaid a planes de cuidado administrado. Si su Medicaid de Florida fue terminado durante o despues de la transicion SMMC 3.0, la razon de terminacion importa para su apelacion. Los errores administrativos durante las transiciones de planes de cuidado administrado han sido una fuente conocida de terminaciones incorrectas.

heading.en: Documents You Need to Enroll After Losing Florida Medicaid in 2026
heading.es: Documentos Necesarios para Inscribirse Despues de Perder Medicaid de Florida en 2026

paragraphs.en: Gathering the right documents before starting your ACA marketplace application at healthcare.gov prevents delays and speeds up verification. Required items include your Florida Medicaid termination notice (shows termination date and reason, this is the qualifying event documentation), Social Security numbers for everyone applying for coverage, recent pay stubs or a tax return to estimate 2026 projected household income, and current Florida mailing address and ZIP code (plan availability varies by county in Florida). If adding dependents: birth certificates for children, and marriage certificate if adding a spouse. For the appeal process at MyACCESS, gather any documents related to the stated reason for termination, income verification, work-requirement compliance records, or proof of documents previously submitted to DCF.
paragraphs.es: Reunir los documentos correctos antes de iniciar su solicitud del mercado ACA en healthcare.gov evita demoras. Los elementos necesarios incluyen su aviso de terminacion de Medicaid de Florida (muestra la fecha de terminacion y la razon, esta es la documentacion del evento calificador), numeros de Seguro Social para todos los que solicitan cobertura, talones de pago recientes o una declaracion de impuestos para estimar el ingreso proyectado del hogar en 2026, y la direccion postal actual en Florida y el codigo ZIP.

list.en: Florida Medicaid termination letter or DCF/AHCA notice (proof of qualifying life event for the 90-day SEP)
list.es: Carta de terminacion de Medicaid de Florida o aviso del DCF/AHCA (prueba del evento calificador de vida para el SEP de 90 dias)

list.es: Numeros de Seguro Social para todos los miembros del hogar que solicitan cobertura

list.es: Talones de pago recientes o la declaracion de impuestos federal mas reciente (Formulario 1040) para el ingreso proyectado en 2026

heading.en: Florida KidCare: Protecting Your Children's Coverage in 2026
heading.es: Florida KidCare: Proteja la Cobertura de Sus Hijos en 2026

paragraphs.en: Florida KidCare is Florida's branded CHIP program for children under 19. KidCare covers children even when the adults in the household are not eligible for Florida Medicaid or marketplace subsidies, making it the most important safety net for families in the Florida coverage gap. Children qualify for Florida KidCare at incomes up to 300% FPL. For 2026, that means $71,820 for a family of 2, $85,410 for a family of 3, and $99,000 for a family of 4. Families between 133% and 200% FPL pay $15 to $20 per month for all eligible children. Above 200% FPL, premiums increase but coverage remains comprehensive. Apply at floridakidcare.org or call 1-888-540-5437. KidCare enrollment is year-round with no SEP deadline, apply at any time.
paragraphs.es: Florida KidCare es el programa CHIP de marca de Florida para ninos menores de 19 anos. KidCare cubre a los ninos incluso cuando los adultos en el hogar no son elegibles para Medicaid de Florida o subsidios del mercado, lo que lo convierte en la red de seguridad mas importante para las familias en la brecha de cobertura de Florida. Los ninos califican para Florida KidCare con ingresos de hasta el 300% FPL. Para 2026, eso significa $71,820 para una familia de 2, $85,410 para una familia de 3 y $99,000 para una familia de 4. Las familias entre el 133% y el 200% FPL pagan de $15 a $20 al mes por todos los ninos elegibles. Solicite en floridakidcare.org o llame al 1-888-540-5437. La inscripcion en KidCare es todo el ano sin fecha limite.

stateRules.rule: Florida has NOT expanded Medicaid under the ACA. Non-parent adults aged 19-64 without qualifying disabilities are categorically ineligible for Florida Medicaid regardless of income. Parents and caretaker relatives are eligible only up to approximately 17% FPL (about $355/month for a single parent in 2026). Pregnant women qualify up to 191% FPL. Children qualify for Medicaid or KidCare CHIP up to 214% FPL through Medicaid and 300% FPL through KidCare.

Florida uses the federally-facilitated marketplace at healthcare.gov, Florida does not have a state-based exchange. Floridians who lose Medicaid use the standard healthcare.gov Marketplace SEP process. Florida had 16 marketplace carriers in 2026, the most of any state.

Florida KidCare (CHIP) covers children under 19 at incomes up to 300% FPL ($99,000 for a family of 4 in 2026). KidCare enrollment is year-round with no deadline. Families between 133% and 200% FPL pay $15-$20/month for all eligible children. Apply at floridakidcare.org.

Florida coverage gap: approximately 800,000 Floridians earn above the Florida Medicaid limit for adults but below 100% FPL, making them ineligible for both Florida Medicaid and ACA marketplace subsidies. The ACA does not offer premium tax credits below 100% FPL in non-expansion states.

en: Applying for ACA marketplace subsidies with income under 100% FPL in Florida, the marketplace will deny PTCs because Florida is a non-expansion state and the ACA requires income at or above 100% FPL for subsidy eligibility
Missing the 90-day SEP window, the clock starts from the Florida Medicaid termination date on your DCF or AHCA notice, not from when you discover the termination
Submitting projected income as last year's full salary instead of current projected income, ACA subsidies are based on expected 2026 household income going forward, which may be significantly lower
Applying without the Florida Medicaid termination letter, healthcare.gov requires documentation of the qualifying event within 30 days of plan selection

Enrolling a child in an ACA marketplace plan when Florida KidCare offers free or near-free coverage for the same child, KidCare at floridakidcare.org covers children up to 300% FPL and is almost always cheaper than adding a child to an adult ACA marketplace plan

Perder la ventana SEP de 90 dias, el reloj comienza desde la fecha de terminacion de Medicaid de Florida en su aviso del DCF o AHCA, no desde cuando descubre la terminacion

Presentar el ingreso proyectado como el salario completo del ano pasado en lugar del ingreso actual proyectado, los subsidios del ACA se basan en el ingreso esperado del hogar en 2026, que puede ser significativamente menor
Solicitar sin la carta de terminacion de Medicaid de Florida, healthcare.gov requiere documentacion del evento calificador dentro de los 30 dias de la seleccion del plan
Inscribir a un nino en un plan del mercado ACA cuando Florida KidCare ofrece cobertura gratuita o casi gratuita para el mismo nino, KidCare en floridakidcare.org cubre ninos hasta el 300% FPL

heading.en: ACA Marketplace vs. Florida Coverage Gap vs. Florida KidCare: Which Path Is Yours?
heading.es: Mercado ACA vs. Brecha de Cobertura de Florida vs. Florida KidCare: Cual Es Su Camino?

body.en: Florida's non-expansion status divides people who lose Medicaid into three distinct situations. Adults earning between 100% and 400% FPL ($15,060 to $60,240 single in 2026) can use the 90-day SEP to enroll at healthcare.gov and typically pay $0 to $200 per month after standard premium tax credits on a Silver plan, and cost-sharing reductions further cut deductibles for incomes under 250% FPL ($37,650 single). At the end of the year, the Marketplace will issue Form 1095-A showing your coverage months and premium tax credit amounts for tax reconciliation on your federal return. Adults earning above 400% FPL pay full marketplace premiums ($400 to $900+ per month individual) because the enhanced PTC cliff returned January 1, 2026. COBRA continuation coverage is typically not relevant for people losing Medicaid (Medicaid is not employer-sponsored coverage), but if you simultaneously had an employer plan and are now losing both job and Medicaid, COBRA charges 102% of the full employer-plan premium and is almost always more expensive than an ACA marketplace plan with subsidies. Adults earning under 100% FPL who are not parents, pregnant, or disabled fall into the Florida coverage gap, and the practical option is a Federally Qualified Health Center on a sliding-fee scale. For children in any of these situations, Florida KidCare (CHIP) at floridakidcare.org covers kids up to 300% FPL at $0 to $20 per month for families between 133% and 200% FPL, making KidCare almost always the first move when adults lose Florida Medicaid.
body.es: El estatus de no expansion de Florida divide a las personas que pierden Medicaid en tres situaciones distintas. Los adultos que ganan entre el 100% y el 400% FPL ($15,060 a $60,240 individual en 2026) pueden usar el SEP de 90 dias para inscribirse en healthcare.gov y generalmente pagan de $0 a $200 al mes despues de creditos fiscales de prima estandar en un plan Silver. Los adultos que ganan por encima del 400% FPL pagan primas completas del mercado ($400 a $900+ al mes individual) porque el acantilado de PTC mejorado regreso el 1 de enero de 2026. Los adultos que ganan bajo el 100% FPL que no son padres, mujeres embarazadas o discapacitados caen en la brecha de cobertura de Florida. Para los ninos en cualquiera de estas situaciones, Florida KidCare (CHIP) en floridakidcare.org cubre a los ninos hasta el 300% FPL a $0 a $20 al mes para familias entre el 133% y el 200% FPL.

en.question: How long do I have to enroll in an ACA plan after losing Florida Medicaid?
en.answer: You have 90 days from the date your Florida Medicaid coverage ended to enroll in an ACA marketplace plan at healthcare.gov. This is longer than the standard 60-day SEP for other coverage losses. Log in to healthcare.gov, select 'I lost qualifying health coverage,' choose Medicaid or CHIP as the type, and enter your Florida Medicaid termination date. Your 90-day clock starts from that termination date, not when you received the notice.

en.question: Does Florida have Medicaid expansion? What is the Florida coverage gap?
en.answer: Florida has not expanded Medicaid under the ACA. Florida Medicaid for adults in 2026 is limited to parents and caretaker relatives earning under approximately 17% FPL (about $355 per month), pregnant women under 191% FPL, and people with qualifying disabilities. Non-parent adults aged 19-64 without disabilities are categorically ineligible regardless of income. The Florida coverage gap refers to approximately 800,000 Floridians who earn above the Medicaid limit but below 100% FPL, they do not qualify for Florida Medicaid or ACA marketplace subsidies.

en.question: What if my income is under 100% FPL in Florida after losing Medicaid?
en.answer: Adults in the Florida coverage gap (under 100% FPL and not a parent, pregnant, or disabled) face limited options. ACA marketplace subsidies require income at or above 100% FPL in non-expansion states like Florida. Practical options include Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs) that offer sliding-scale primary care, call 211 to locate the nearest FQHC in Florida. Emergency Medicaid covers true emergencies. If your income increases above 100% FPL, you can enroll in a marketplace plan with subsidies at healthcare.gov.

en.question: Can I appeal a Florida Medicaid termination?
en.answer: Yes. Florida allows 90 days from the notice date to request a fair hearing. Call DCF at (850) 300-4323 or submit a fair hearing request through your MyACCESS account at myaccess.myflfamilies.com. If you request the hearing before your coverage ends, you may be entitled to continuation of benefits during the appeal process. File your appeal AND apply for ACA marketplace coverage simultaneously through healthcare.gov, do not wait for the appeal outcome.

en.question: What is Florida KidCare and how does it help after losing Medicaid?
en.answer: Florida KidCare is Florida's CHIP program covering children under 19 at incomes up to 300% FPL, $99,000 for a family of 4 in 2026. KidCare enrollment is year-round with no SEP deadline. Families between 133% and 200% FPL pay just $15 to $20 per month for all eligible children. Even if you as an adult fall into the Florida coverage gap, your children can enroll in KidCare any time at floridakidcare.org or by calling 1-888-540-5437.

en.question: What is the 2026 subsidy cliff and how does it affect Florida marketplace plans?
en.answer: The 2026 subsidy cliff means that ACA premium tax credits cut off abruptly at 400% FPL ($60,240 for a single person in 2026). Enhanced premium tax credits from the American Rescue Plan Act and Inflation Reduction Act expired January 1, 2026. If your income is between 100% and 400% FPL, standard PTCs still apply. If your income is above 400% FPL, you pay full marketplace premiums, typically $400 to $900 or more per month for individual coverage in Florida in 2026.

en.question: What documents do I need to enroll in ACA marketplace coverage after losing Florida Medicaid?
en.answer: Required documents for your healthcare.gov application include your Florida Medicaid termination letter or DCF/AHCA written notice (this is your qualifying event documentation), Social Security numbers for all household members, recent pay stubs or tax return to estimate 2026 projected income, and your Florida ZIP code (plans vary by county). For children, have birth certificates ready. You must upload your termination notice to healthcare.gov within 30 days of selecting a plan to complete verification.

en.question: What if I miss the 90-day SEP after losing Florida Medicaid?
en.answer: Missing the 90-day SEP window after losing Florida Medicaid means you generally must wait until the next Open Enrollment Period, November 1, 2026 through January 15, 2027 for coverage starting in 2027. One exception: if another qualifying life event occurs (job change, marriage, birth, move to a new county with different plan availability), you get a new Special Enrollment Period. Children can always enroll in Florida KidCare year-round regardless of missed SEP windows.

es.question: Cuanto tiempo tengo para inscribirme en un plan ACA despues de perder Medicaid de Florida?
es.answer: Tiene 90 dias desde la fecha en que termino su cobertura de Medicaid de Florida para inscribirse en un plan del mercado ACA en healthcare.gov. Esto es mas largo que el SEP estandar de 60 dias para otras perdidas de cobertura. Inicie sesion en healthcare.gov, seleccione 'Perdi cobertura medica calificada', elija Medicaid o CHIP como tipo y escriba la fecha de terminacion de su Medicaid de Florida. Su reloj de 90 dias comienza desde esa fecha de terminacion.

es.question: Florida tiene expansion de Medicaid? Que es la brecha de cobertura de Florida?
es.answer: Florida no ha expandido Medicaid bajo el ACA. El Medicaid de Florida para adultos en 2026 se limita a padres y cuidadores con ingresos bajo aproximadamente el 17% FPL (cerca de $355 al mes), mujeres embarazadas bajo el 191% FPL, y personas con discapacidades calificadoras. Los adultos sin hijos de 19 a 64 anos sin discapacidades estan categoricamente excluidos independientemente de sus ingresos. La brecha de cobertura de Florida se refiere a aproximadamente 800,000 floridanos que ganan por encima del limite de Medicaid pero bajo el 100% FPL.

es.question: Que pasa si mis ingresos estan bajo el 100% FPL en Florida despues de perder Medicaid?
es.answer: Los adultos en la brecha de cobertura de Florida (bajo el 100% FPL y no son padres, mujeres embarazadas o discapacitados) tienen opciones limitadas. Los subsidios del mercado ACA requieren ingresos del 100% FPL o mas en estados sin expansion como Florida. Las opciones practicas incluyen los Centros de Salud Comunitarios Calificados Federalmente (FQHC) que ofrecen atencion primaria a escala de honorarios reducidos, llame al 211 para localizar el FQHC mas cercano en Florida.

es.question: Puedo apelar una terminacion de Medicaid de Florida?
es.answer: Si. Florida permite 90 dias desde la fecha del aviso para solicitar una audiencia justa. Llame al DCF al (850) 300-4323 o presente una solicitud de audiencia justa a traves de su cuenta MyACCESS en myaccess.myflfamilies.com. Si solicita la audiencia antes de que termine su cobertura, puede tener derecho a continuacion de beneficios durante el proceso de apelacion. Presente su apelacion Y solicite cobertura del mercado ACA a traves de healthcare.gov al mismo tiempo.

es.question: Que es Florida KidCare y como ayuda despues de perder Medicaid?
es.answer: Florida KidCare es el programa CHIP de Florida que cubre a ninos menores de 19 con ingresos de hasta el 300% FPL, $99,000 para una familia de 4 en 2026. La inscripcion en KidCare es todo el ano sin fecha limite de SEP. Las familias entre el 133% y el 200% FPL pagan solo $15 a $20 al mes por todos los ninos elegibles. Incluso si usted como adulto cae en la brecha de cobertura de Florida, sus hijos pueden inscribirse en KidCare en cualquier momento en floridakidcare.org o llamando al 1-888-540-5437.

es.question: Que es el acantilado de subsidios 2026 y como afecta los planes del mercado de Florida?
es.answer: El acantilado de subsidios 2026 significa que los creditos fiscales de prima del ACA se cortan abruptamente al 400% FPL ($60,240 para una persona sola en 2026). Los creditos fiscales de prima mejorados del ARPA y la IRA expiraron el 1 de enero de 2026. Si su ingreso esta entre el 100% y el 400% FPL, los PTC estandar aun aplican. Si su ingreso esta por encima del 400% FPL, paga primas completas del mercado, tipicamente $400 a $900 o mas al mes por cobertura individual en Florida en 2026.

es.question: Que documentos necesito para inscribirme en cobertura del mercado ACA despues de perder Medicaid de Florida?
es.answer: Los documentos requeridos para su solicitud en healthcare.gov incluyen su carta de terminacion de Medicaid de Florida o aviso escrito del DCF/AHCA (esta es su documentacion de evento calificador), numeros de Seguro Social para todos los miembros del hogar, talones de pago recientes o declaracion de impuestos para estimar el ingreso proyectado en 2026, y su codigo ZIP de Florida. Para ninos, tenga actas de nacimiento listas. Debe subir su aviso de terminacion a healthcare.gov dentro de los 30 dias de seleccionar un plan.

es.question: Que pasa si pierdo la ventana SEP de 90 dias despues de perder Medicaid de Florida?
es.answer: Perder la ventana SEP de 90 dias despues de perder Medicaid de Florida significa que generalmente debe esperar hasta el siguiente Periodo de Inscripcion Abierta, del 1 de noviembre de 2026 al 15 de enero de 2027 para cobertura que comienza en 2027. Una excepcion: si ocurre otro evento calificador (cambio de trabajo, matrimonio, nacimiento, mudanza a un nuevo condado con diferente disponibilidad de planes), obtiene un nuevo Periodo de Inscripcion Especial. Los ninos siempre pueden inscribirse en Florida KidCare todo el ano.
